title: HP Raises Outlook as Premium AI PCs and Tariff Refunds Boost Results
excerpt: HP (NYSE:HPQ) Chief Financial Officer Karen Parkhill said the company’s third-quarter performance was supported by record revenue in its Personal Systems seg...
content_html:
MarketBeat

Sun, September 13, 2026 at 8:01 AM PDT 6 min read

Key Points

  • Interested in HP Inc.? Here are five stocks we like better.

  • HP raised its annual outlook after record Personal Systems revenue, premium product mix, pricing actions and tariff refunds boosted third-quarter results. The company expects an additional tariff-refund benefit in the fourth quarter, but its guidance increase excludes that benefit.

  • Demand is shifting toward premium AI PCs, workstations and hybrid AI solutions that run workloads locally and in the cloud. HP expects Personal Systems margins to dip in the fourth quarter before gradually returning to its long-term 5%–7% range in fiscal 2027.

  • HP is expanding growth initiatives in Print, including Big Tank, industrial and 3D printing, while Big Tank gained four points of market share. Print margins are expected at the low end of the 16%–19% target range due to unit placements and higher input costs.

  • MarketBeat Week in Review – 03/30 - 04/03

HP (NYSE:HPQ) Chief Financial Officer Karen Parkhill said the company's third-quarter performance was supported by record revenue in its Personal Systems segment, premium product mix and pricing actions, while Print results met expectations. Speaking at the Goldman Sachs Communacopia + Technology Conference, Parkhill said the company raised its annual guidance even excluding the benefit of tariff refunds.

Parkhill said HP continued to execute its four-pillar plan for managing higher commodity costs, which includes securing supply, shaping demand, reducing costs and implementing pricing actions. The company also benefited from refunds of IEEPA tariffs during the third quarter and expects additional refunds in the fourth quarter.

Premium PCs and Hybrid AI Demand

→ IBM and Lockheed Martin Turn a Swiss Defense Deal Into a Quantum Computing Bet

  • HP Inc. Stock Is Historically Cheap, but Can AI Change the Story?

HP is focusing its Personal Systems strategy on premium commercial PCs, AI PCs, workstations, peripherals and service offerings, including its Workforce Experience Platform, or WXP. Parkhill said the strategy is intended to expand market share, drive revenue growth and improve the company's sales mix and margins.

The company is seeing growth across regions and regained market leadership in the Americas and North America during the latest quarter, Parkhill said.

→ Kroger's Textbook Entry for Buy-and-Hold Investors

  • HP Is Positioning Itself for the AI Gold Rush's Second Act

While early demand for AI PCs was driven in part by customers seeking to future-proof their technology fleets, Parkhill said enterprise customers are increasingly seeking solutions that allow artificial intelligence workloads to run locally as well as in the cloud.
